notes: Asserts the row's core claim for gemini-cli: a permission dialog raised by a READ-ONLY tool produces its own waiting episode, identical to one raised by a mutating tool. WHY THIS IS OBSERVABLE AT ALL: gemini-cli's resolveConfirmation calls notifyHooks(deps, details) unconditionally, immediately after shouldConfirmExecute returns details and BEFORE it parks the call at awaiting_approval and blocks. Nothing on that path reads the tool name or class, so a web_fetch (type:'info', title 'Confirm Web Fetch') confirmation emits the same Notification/ToolPermission hook a run_shell_command (type:'exec') one does. irrlicht's geminicli receiver holds SignalPermissionPrompt on that hook (-> PermissionPending -> waiting), AfterTool releases it (-> working), and AfterAgent calls HandleStopHook plus an unconditional ReleasePermissionPromptHold (-> ready). THE TOOL PAIR: policies/write.toml gates web_fetch at decision=ask_user in the same block as run_shell_command / write_file / replace, while policies/read-only.toml allows glob/grep_search/list_directory/read_file/google_web_search - so web_fetch is the read-only tool gated in DEFAULT mode, and no configuration beyond DEFAULT approval mode is needed. TWO TURNS, NOT ONE: the arc below carries an extra ready in the middle (turn1_end) because the recipe drives one gated call per turn. That is deliberate and the scenario permits it - irrlicht's SignalPermissionPrompt is a single per-session hold and AfterTool releases it broadly, so two simultaneously-open confirmations would merge into ONE waiting episode and the first tool's AfterTool would release the hold while the second dialog was still on screen. Merging is precisely what this row forbids, so the extra ready is the price of keeping the two episodes separately attributable. BIRTH ANCHORING: gemini-cli is a presession adapter, but its birth ORDER is a race, not a fixed presession-then-session sequence - across four committed gemini-cli recordings the real transcript session appears first in three (2-3, 2-16, 1-3, 2-8) and the proc-<PID> row first in one (2-4). So the codex-style two-phase presession_birth/session_birth form is NOT used here: it would pin session_birth to whichever row happened to lose the race. Instead session_birth anchors to start UNPINNED and no later phase carries same_session_as - the form every green gemini-cli spec already uses, and the form that survives either ordering because the proc-<PID> row never goes working. NO max_delay_ms ON EITHER waiting PHASE: gemini-cli hooks are beacon-delivered (irrlichd hook-post gemini-cli re-resolves the daemon address per fire) and that per-fire process spawn was not timed. Record may add a ceiling once a real latency is measured. observations.model is inherited from the 2-17 recording, where record settled gemini-3.5-flash live on the API-key tier (correcting an earlier doc-derived gemini-3-flash-preview); still record-correctable. PROVISIONAL: nothing here was live-confirmed - this host cannot make gemini model calls (IneligibleTierError), so daemon=full is a two-sided source read, not a recording.

text: A gemini-cli session appears in ready shortly after launch. Anchored to start UNPINNED so whichever of the transcript session / proc-<PID> row wins the birth race can satisfy it.
The launcher PID is bound by cwd (harvested from the bootstrap <session_context>, since gemini's cwd lives only in the transcript body); the heap-bump worker is excluded.
Turn 1's prompt (the MUTATING half: run_shell_command) drives ready -> working.

The mutating tool's confirmation opens and the session goes working -> waiting. This half is the path tool-gate-permission-prompt already covers; it is here as the control the read-only half is compared against.
The user answers the dialog (Allow once, option index 0); the approved tool runs and its AfterTool releases the permission-prompt hold -> working.
AfterAgent closes turn 1 -> ready. This ready is an artifact of driving the two calls in separate turns, not part of the scenario's own arc.
Turn 2's prompt (the READ-ONLY half: web_fetch) drives ready -> working.

THE PHASE THIS ROW EXISTS FOR. The READ-ONLY tool's dialog ('Confirm Web Fetch') produces its OWN waiting episode - not skipped, and not merged into the mutating tool's episode, which ended a full turn earlier. A recording in which this phase is missing while mutating_gate_waiting passed is exactly the #1861 shape: the gate reaching the daemon for one tool class and not the other.
The user answers the second dialog; web_fetch runs and its AfterTool releases the hold -> working.
AfterAgent closes turn 2 -> ready. The session does not remain waiting after the last dialog closes.

The session is still ready across the >=10s trailing idle - it was not left pinned at waiting by a hold that nothing retired. AfterAgent's unconditional ReleasePermissionPromptHold is what this phase checks; without it a cancelled confirmation would sit held until SignalPermissionPrompt's 12-hour ceiling.
